item.title: Cost of Living in Niddrie Melbourne
item.description:
Rent in Niddrie tells one story. Groceries, coffee, and parking tell another. Here is the full picture.

Read our full Niddrie suburb guide for the bigger picture.

Is Niddrie Expensive?

Niddrie sits somewhere in the middle of Melbourne’s cost spectrum. It’s not cheap, but it’s not going to break the bank either — assuming you’re realistic about expectations.

The cost of living here reflects what the suburb offers. Location, community, access to amenities — you get what you pay for, and in Niddrie, you’re generally getting good value for the price point.

item.title: Getting Around Niddrie — Transport Guide
item.description:
The commute question is make-or-break for most people considering Niddrie. Let us cut through the fluff.

Check out our full Niddrie suburb guide for the complete picture.

Getting Around Niddrie — The Quick Version

Public transport in Niddrie is decent. You can get to the city in roughly 30 to 50 minutes during peak hours. Having a car helps, especially for weekend errands and trips outside the PT network.

Train Access

Niddrie is served by train, though you may need to get to the nearest station which can be a short walk or bus ride away.

item.title: Niddrie Neighbourhood Guide — Streets and Pockets
item.description:
Niddrie isn’t one monolithic block. Like most Melbourne suburbs, it has different pockets with different personalities. Here’s how to read the suburb from the inside.

See our full Niddrie suburb guide for the overview.

Niddrie Isn’t Just One Thing

Walk from one end of Niddrie to the other and you’ll notice the vibe shift. The main commercial strip has one energy. The residential streets behind it have another. And the edges of the suburb — where it bleeds into Essendon North — have their own thing going on.
